bd-5ljt6 (P2, decision) — NEW, and it is the conclusion four nights of report-only notes kept circling without drawing. board-scan Scan B's plan status vocabulary is draft|refined|approved|beadified|loop-ready and the snapshot it returns has exactly those 5 buckets. A plan whose frontmatter status is OUTSIDE that set lands in NO bucket and is dropped from the plans board of every consumer (ac-align, ac-human-session, ac-dashboard, ac-loop orient, ac-tidy). Scan B's fallback ladder only fires when frontmatter is ABSENT — present-but-out-of-vocabulary is an unhandled third case that looks well-formed and vanishes silently. 2 of 4 active plans (50%) are in that state: post-cleanup-backlog-handoff (status: open) and the new curator-tie-break-policy (status: awaiting-ratification). The second is the sharper case — a decision doc whose whole purpose is ratification, invisible to the very surface that would raise it to a human; reachable only via bd-ea8yb. ac-tidy cannot self-heal it because Phase 2e's condition is 'plans LACKING frontmatter'. Framed as a fork: (A) recommended, add a fail-loud unclassified[] catch-all to Scan B so nothing is ever invisible again, reported by ac-dashboard/ac-tidy on the same rule Scan D's staleness already follows; (B) complementary, file non-plan docs under _plans/decisions/ so the vocabulary stops widening; (C) rejected, map stragglers onto existing buckets (semantically false, re-hides the problem). Explicitly cross-referenced to bd-m64d5 (P1) as the SAME defect family — that is Scan C's zero-checkbox silent drop, this is Scan B's equivalent, so board-scan has two independent silent-drop paths in two different scans and the general principle (a read layer must never silently drop an item it cannot classify) is the real fix. Nothing auto-applied: no plan file was edited, moved or re-statused, since the status values are deliberate authorial choices and rewriting them is precisely the heuristic-not-provable move the guardrails forbid.
